accessibilityGrantState.beforeAndDuring: Two distinct responsible identities were exercised. Under the root / ChatGPT responsible identity the real check returned trusted. Under the Claude Code and Claude Opus 5 launched probe processes the real check returned notTrusted, both while the System Settings Accessibility toggle named lowercase 'claude' was on and after it was restored to off.
accessibilityGrantState.conclusion: The lowercase 'claude' UI row was not the effective TCC responsible identity of the Swift test process, so no grant or revoke transition was demonstrated for that process. Recorded as a Tier-H limitation in manual.md and in commands.json manualProbeCommands.reviewerRuns.
accessibilityGrantState.toggleHandling: The reviewer switched that toggle from off to on after explicit owner authorization and Touch ID, and restored it to off afterwards. The system was left in its original state.

authorEnvironmentLimitations.swiftPackageManagerSandbox: SwiftPM manifest evaluation fails in this session with 'sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted'. It reproduces on an unmodified export of the base commit and persists even when the outer harness sandbox is disabled, so it is a property of the host session and not of this change. Exact SwiftPM Required Command forms are therefore non-authoritative here; --disable-sandbox equivalents were run instead and are labelled as such in commands.json.
authorEnvironmentLimitations.xcodebuildWorkspace: xcodebuild reports "'MacKVM.xcworkspace' is not a workspace file" (exit 66). It reproduces identically on a pristine git archive export of base commit c26240787447a911209867611c0210ec0fa7f428 in /tmp, so it is environmental and pre-existing. The workspace files are untouched by this Issue.
authorEnvironmentLimitations.consequence: No blocked command is claimed as passing on the strength of an author run. Every one of them has since been reported as passing by the reviewer in its exact frozen form; see commands.json reviewerFinalResults.
